messages:
maria: Heads up — sudden hot burst hitting eastus2 chat-infer, GPU pools at ~96% and a bunch of pods are Pending. Autoscaler didn't add capacity as expected.
metrics-bot: ALERT: cluster-eastus2/gpu-utilization=92% (5m), pending_pods=118, scale_attempts_failed=3 :rotating_light:
lucas: Oncall here, looking. maria can you paste the first ScaleUp error from the provisioner/controller logs?
maria: controller logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-20T14:23:12Z] provisioner: ScaleUp request for nodegroup gpu-nodepool-us-east2
[2026-03-20T14:23:12Z] provisioner: ScaleUp failed: NodeCreateError: detected tombstoned instances, deferring replacement for 10m
[2026-03-20T14:23:42Z] provisioner: CapacityRequest returned: ASG.Throttled
```
tim: We pushed a GPU driver + AMI rotation last night. Could be a bad image causing nodes to be tombstoned on boot.
anya: We did a canary of the image on a small subset, but there was a partial rollout to us-east2 — @deploy-bot confirm rollout state.
deploy-bot: Rollout 1092: image-gpu-v3 -> started 2026-03-20T02:00Z, completed on us-east2 nodes: partial (60% nodes upgraded), hooks: restart-kubelet applied.
lucas: kubelet logs show repeated `container runtime not ready` on newly created nodes. New nodes are getting `provisioner/tombstoned` taint.
maria: kubectl outputs:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending
chat-infer-5xx   Pending   0/1   1 GPU required
$ kubectl describe node gpu-node-az1 | grep -A2 Taints
Taints: provisioner/tombstoned:NoExecute
```
tim: Autoscaler/provisioner is intentionally deferring replacing tombstoned nodes for 10m to avoid thrash from transient boot faults. But with a hot burst that deferral is blocking scale-up decisions.
lucas: I'm seeing ScaleUp loop: controller requests +12 nodes -> cloud returns throttled or tombstone detected -> controller backs off. Net result: scale-up lag ~4m and pod queue builds up.
sre-rookie: Can we temporarily bump max nodes or bypass tombstone deferral to cut the queue?
anya: Approve emergency: bump max nodes by 30% for 30m and allow provisioner to ignore tombstone deferral for surge path. @lucas coordinate and document.
lucas: Manually increased nodepool max by +30%. Also removing `provisioner/tombstoned` label from 2 nodes that look healthy but were auto-tainted during the rollout.
metrics-bot: scale_event: nodepool-us-east2 requested +12, 8 became Ready, 4 stuck (AttachVolume errors).
maria: Started traffic reroute to us-west1 for non-low-latency routes to relieve eastus2.
sre-rookie: Is disabling tombstone deferral safe? Could reintroduce thrash if image is actually bad.
tim: Temporary override in controller: set `tombstone_deferral_seconds=0` for surge path; monitoring closely. Also initiating rollback for image-gpu-v3.
deploy-bot: Rollout 1092 rollback initiated -> target: image-gpu-v2 at 2026-03-20T15:05Z.
maria: After override and max bump, pod Pending count dropped to 18 and p95 latency is stabilizing. Still watching for AttachVolume failures on 4 nodes.
anya: Post-incident follow-ups: (1) add a surge bypass that temporarily tolerates tombstoned nodes if cluster-wide GPU utilization > 85%, (2) improve image rollout gating so AMI/driver mismatches don't partial-roll, (3) add playbook step to increase max nodes as emergency path.
lucas: I'll attach logs and a timeline to the incident ticket. Thanks all for quick ops. :thumbsup:
__notes: This thread captures an autoscaler/provisioner failure during a sudden GPU load spike with tombstoned nodes and deferral logic causing scale-up lag; includes short logs and operational coordination.
